R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) placed after credential verification and before session state is written; nothing else in the handler changes.

R582.note: One-token change of mux to protectedHandler on the plaintext listener; GET routes are unaffected since CrossOriginProtection only guards unsafe methods.

R583.note: createCipheriv with PBKDF2-derived key and random IV/salt is the right replacement; the response gains iv and salt fields, stated plainly and needed for decryption (synchronous 100k-iteration KDF in the request path is a throughput cost, not a weakness).

R584.note: Dropping decoder.Entity closes it, but any partner document that references ¬eLabel; now fails to decode and gets 400, and the write-up asserts the opposite ('does not affect the core functionality').

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') replaces Math.random(); only the code's length/alphabet changes, which is inherent to the fix.

R586.note: fgets closes the stack overflow but adds no truncation check: an over-long line is silently truncated and returned as success (0) instead of -1, and its tail stays queued in stdin to corrupt the next call - both points the stated contract explicitly requires, and neither is mentioned (fgets returning NULL is also unchecked, so strlen can read uninitialised stack).

R587.note: Build FAIL - IAntiforgery is used without 'using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery;'; otherwise the shape is right, though a handler-thrown AntiforgeryValidationException surfaces as 500 rather than 400, and a build break is loud rather than silent.

R588.note: exp4j does close code execution, but it has no comparison or ternary operators, so the class's own documented formula shape 'basePrice * (quantity > 10 ? 0.9 : 1.0)' now throws and the blanket catch silently returns basePrice - wrong prices with no error - while the write-up claims those operators are supported; results also now round-trip through double instead of staying BigDecimal.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset and returns the captured value; the returned number is the same one the function's comment promises and nothing else moves.

R590.note: Textbook PreparedStatement with a bound parameter; only nit is setString against an apparently numeric id column, which some drivers type-check more strictly than the original unquoted literal.

R591.note: Manual quoting of an argument passed to a .bat, which CreateProcess re-enters through cmd.exe - balanced quote doubling happens to keep cmd's quote parity so metacharacters stay inert, but the stated rationale is wrong (cmd escapes with ^, not "") and the right shape here is ArgumentList / not re-entering cmd, and % expansion is still live; the script's %2 now arrives wrapped in quotes with inner quotes doubled, an unstated change to what the batch file sees.

R592.note: Does not close the vector: SLF4J's {} placeholders only defer string building, they do not escape CR/LF in the substituted value, so the injected newline still reaches the log; the write-up's claim that the logger 'automatically escapes control characters' is false. Contract is otherwise preserved - the trailing Throwable is still attached and 401 still returned.

R593.note: Path.GetFileName plus an extension allowlist is a workable CWE-434 shape, but the allowlist rejects types the endpoint previously accepted (.csv, .zip, anything outside the eight listed) with a new 400 body; stated, so 1 rather than 0.

R594.note: csrf-csrf doubleCsrf with getSessionIdentifier is the right maintained middleware and the 401/403 shapes survive, but getSecret falls back to a hardcoded 'default-secret-change-me' when the env var is unset, and no token-issuing route is added, so no legitimate client can obtain a token - neither is called out.

R595.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus GUID rename is a strong closure, but it narrows accepted uploads to PNG/JPEG/GIF/PDF, adds a 10 MB cap, and changes the returned 'stored' name from the client's filename to a GUID; all disclosed, so 1 rather than 0.
